questions.question: Explain the principle of the Bridgman technique in crystal growth.
questions.solution_html:
• The Bridgman technique is a method for growing large single crystals from a molten charge, based on controlled
  • directional solidification.In the Bridgman method, the molten material is slowly cooled so that it solidifies
  • gradually from one end to the other inside a container (crucible).A temperature gradient is maintained — one end
  • of the furnace is hotter (above melting point) and the other is cooler (below melting point).As the crucible is slowly
  • moved from the hot zone to the cool zone, the melt solidifies progressively, allowing the formation of a single
  • large crystal along the length of the container, guided by the controlled temperature gradient.
  • Principle -(1mark) Explanation-(2marks)
  • Short Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Short Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write an essay on how simple distillation illustrates the principle of volatility differences.
questions.solution_html:
• volatility differences.
  • Simple Distillation is based on the fundamental principle that different substances have different boiling points
  • and volatilities. The process of simple distillation exploits these differences. When a liquid mixture is heated, the
  • component with the lower boiling point (higher volatility) vaporizes first. This vapour, when condensed, forms a
  • distillate that is richer in the more volatile component. The operation of simple distillation clearly demonstrates
  • that the separation of components is possible only if there is a sufficient difference in their boiling points — usually
  • at least 25–30°C.For example, when a mixture of acetone (b.p. 56°C) and water (b.p. 100°C) is distilled, acetone
  • being more volatile, vaporizes first and condenses as the distillate, leaving water behind.
  • Principle -(2 marks) Relevant explanation with any example-(5marks)
questions.final_answer: Option (c) For example, when a mixture of acetone (b.p. 56°C) and water (b.p. 100°C) is distilled, acetone
